name: Genetic 46,XY Difference of Sex Development of Endocrine Origin
aliases: 46,XY Disorder of Sex Development due to Endocrine Abnormality

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Statement on Management of Differences of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XY karyotype confirmed by cytogenetic analysis
Biochemical evidence of impaired androgen synthesis or action
Clinical presentation with ambiguous or atypical external genitalia
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex steroid biosynthesis or androgen receptor function
Imaging evidence of gonadal dysgenesis or abnormal gonadal location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XY karyotype with endocrine dysfunction and ambiguous genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetics, endocrinology, and radiology.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes hypospadias, micropenis, and labioscrotal fusion abnormalities

common.symptomName: Delayed or absent virilization during puberty

occasional.symptomName: Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)

rare.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to steroidogenic enzyme defects
searchTerms: high blood pressure from hormone problems

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations related to gender dysphoria
searchTerms: mental health issues from gender dysphoria
psychiatric symptoms related to gender identity
psychological distress due to gender incongruence

laboratory: Low serum testosterone with elevated LH and FSH
Abnormal steroid hormone profiles (e.g., low dihydrotestosterone)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing gonadal dysgenesis or undescended testes
Pelvic imaging to assess presence or absence of Müllerian structures
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as AR, SRD5A2, HSD17B3, or NR5A1
other: Histopathological examination of gonadal tissue showing dysgenesis or absence of germ cells

distinguishingFeatures: Complete androgen insensitivity presents with female external genitalia despite 46,XY karyotype
Normal or elevated testosterone levels with absent androgen receptor function

redFlags: Severe ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation
Signs of adrenal crisis or salt-wasting
Rapid virilization in infancy or childhood
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of differences of sex development. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2017.
Lee PA, et al. Global DSD update since 2006: management of DSD. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
Orphanet: Genetic 46,XY difference of sex development of endocrine origin (ORPHA:325713)
